newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke-No decisions yet on fx revaluation.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke-No decisions yet on fx revaluation.

text.p: The Bundesbank has signalled to the German government that it would consider revaluing currency reserves but has taken no decision on the level or whether to make a payout to Bonn, a council member said on Tuesday.

"No final decisions have been taken," Ernst Welteke told Reuters in answer to questions about whether the Bundesbank had fixed a level for any revaluation and whether it planned to transfer any profit to the Bonn government.
Government sources have said the Bundesbank would be willing to revalue its dollar reserves to 1.50 marks or even higher.

In an interview with Reuters held early Tuesday morning, Welteke declined to comment on any exact levels, saying the Bundesbank would need to keep a careful eye on the dollar's development and take its decision at some point in the future.

"The central bank council has signalled its willingness to revalue the dollar differently in the 1997 balance sheet, but the council reserves the right to decide how it might use profits that could result from this," Welteke said.
The Bundesbank traditionally transfers a portion of its profits in April to the Bonn government, which uses these to help pare back debt.

Until now the Bundesbank has valued its dollar reserves at historical lows. Welteke said even if the Bundesbank were to revalue currency reserves, it would continue to be very careful, making sure not to assign inappropriate values which would prevent the Bundesbank from suddenly having a loss on its books.
